questions.statement: Which sentence expresses the zero conditional?

options.text: If you had heated ice, it would have melted.
options.feedback: That is the third conditional, referring to an unreal past situation.

options.text: If you heat ice, it would melt.
options.feedback: That is the first conditional, describing a possible future situation.

options.text: If you heat ice, it melts.
options.feedback: 'If' plus present plus present states a general truth.

options.text: If you would heat ice, it melts.
options.feedback: 'Would' after 'if' belongs to a hypothetical conditional, not the zero.

questions.explanation:
El condicional cero expresa una relacion general siempre verdadera: 'If + presente, presente'.

questions.statement: Complete the first conditional: 'If it ____ tomorrow, we will cancel the trip.'

options.text: will rain
options.feedback: 'Will' belongs to the main clause, not to the 'if' clause of this conditional.

options.text: is raining
options.feedback: The present continuous suggests a currently temporary situation, not a future condition.

options.text: rains
options.feedback: 'If it rains' plus 'we will cancel' is the standard first conditional.

options.text: rained
options.feedback: The simple past in the 'if' clause would indicate the third conditional.

questions.explanation:
En el condicional tipo uno la clausula de 'if' va en presente simple y la principal en 'will' mas verbo base.

questions.statement: What does the first conditional express?

options.text: An impossible situation in the past
options.feedback: An unreal past situation is expressed by the third conditional.

options.text: A possible situation and its likely result in the future
options.feedback: That is the meaning of the first conditional.

options.text: A general truth that is always valid
options.feedback: A general truth belongs to the zero conditional.

options.text: A regret about the past
options.feedback: Regret is expressed with 'wish' plus the past perfect.

El condicional tipo uno describe una situacion posible y su consecuencia probable en el futuro.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence expresses the second conditional?

options.text: If I have more time, I would learn another language.
options.feedback: That is the first conditional structure, not the second.

options.text: If I had more time, I would learn another language.
options.feedback: 'If' plus past simple plus 'would' base is the second conditional.

options.text: If I had more time, I will learn another language.
options.feedback: 'Will' does not belong to the second conditional's main clause.

options.text: If I would have more time, I learn another language.
options.feedback: 'Would' cannot follow 'if' in this pattern.

questions.explanation:
El condicional tipo dos usa 'If' mas pasado simple y 'would' mas verbo base para una hipotesis no real del presente.

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that is correct in the third conditional.

options.text: If she studies harder, she would have passed the exam.
options.feedback: That mixes the first conditional's 'if' clause with the third's main clause.

options.text: If she had studied harder, she will have passed the exam.
options.feedback: 'Will have' does not belong to the third conditional.

options.text: If she would have studied, she would have passed the exam.
options.feedback: 'Would have' cannot be used in the 'if' clause of the third conditional.

options.text: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
options.feedback: 'Had studied' plus 'would have passed' is the third conditional.

questions.explanation:
El condicional tipo tres emplea 'If' mas pasado perfecto y 'would have' mas participio.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'If I ____ you, I would accept the offer.'

options.text: am
options.feedback: 'Am' is the simple present of 'to be', which does not fit the hypothetical structure.

options.text: was
options.feedback: 'Was' is used with he, she and it, but 'I' takes 'were' in this conditional.

options.text: were
options.feedback: 'Were' is the standard form in the second conditional for every person.

options.text: will be
options.feedback: 'Will be' does not appear in the 'if' clause of the second conditional.

questions.explanation:
En el condicional tipo dos se usa 'were' para todas las personas, incluso para 'I'. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the difference between the first and the second conditional?

options.text: Both express the same probability
options.feedback: The two conditionals differ precisely in how likely they consider the situation.

options.text: The first is a likely future possibility; the second is a hypothetical one
options.feedback: The distinction is real likelihood versus imagined situation.

options.text: The first refers to the past and the second to the present
options.feedback: The first is about the future; the third, not the second, is about the past.

options.text: The second is used only in questions
options.feedback: Both appear in statements and in questions.

questions.explanation:
El tipo uno trata de una posibilidad real en el futuro; el tipo dos, de una hipotesis menos probable o imaginaria en el presente.

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'If it will rain, we will stay home.' What is the error?

options.text: Nothing is wrong with the sentence
options.feedback: Some informal speech allows it, but the standard school form excludes 'will' after 'if'.

options.text: 'Stay' must be 'stayed'
options.feedback: 'Will stay' is the correct form for the main clause.

options.text: 'Rain' must be 'rained'
options.feedback: The verb must be in the present simple without the -ed ending.

options.text: 'If' plus 'will' is incorrect; it should be 'If it rains'
options.feedback: The 'if' clause of the first conditional uses the present simple.

questions.explanation:
En el condicional tipo uno la clausula de 'if' no lleva 'will'; se usa el presente simple.

questions.statement: Read the text: 'If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.' What type of conditional is this?

options.text: The zero conditional, because it states a general truth
options.feedback: 'If' plus present plus present expresses an always valid rule.

options.text: The first conditional, because it refers to the future
options.feedback: No future time is mentioned; the statement is always true.

options.text: The second conditional, because it is hypothetical
options.feedback: The second conditional describes an unreal present situation.

options.text: The third conditional, because it refers to the past
options.feedback: No past event appears in the sentence.

questions.explanation:
La oracion expresa una relacion cientifica siempre verdadera, que corresponde al condicional cero.

options.text: am
options.feedback: 'Am' is the simple present of 'to be' with 'I'.

options.text: will be
options.feedback: 'Will be' belongs to the first conditional's main clause.

options.text: were
options.feedback: 'Were' is the form used for every person in the second conditional.

options.text: had been

La hipotesis del condicional tipo dos se enuncia con el pasado simple del verbo 'be'.

options.text: will have
options.feedback: 'Will have' belongs to the future perfect, not to this conditional.

options.text: have
options.feedback: The present 'have' would make this the first conditional.

questions.statement: Which sentence expresses a regret about a past action?
questions.context: Uso de 'wish' para el arrepentimiento, Guayaquil.

options.text: I wish I would book the flight earlier.
options.feedback: 'Would' plus base form expresses a future wish, not past regret.

options.text: I wish I had booked the flight earlier.
options.feedback: 'Wish' plus past perfect expresses regret about a past action.

options.text: I wish I have booked the flight earlier.
options.feedback: The present perfect does not combine with 'wish' for past regret.

options.text: I wish the flight would be booked earlier.
options.feedback: That construction does not express the standard regret pattern.

'Wish' mas pasado perfecto expresa el deseo de que algo pasado hubiera ocurrido. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does 'would' express in the sentence 'If she studied more, she would improve'?

options.text: A hypothetical result that may not happen
options.feedback: 'Would' marks the consequence of an imagined condition.

options.text: A certain future event
options.feedback: Certainty would require the first conditional with 'will'.

options.text: A past event
options.feedback: The whole conditional is oriented to the present, not the past.

options.text: An obligation
options.feedback: Obligation would be expressed with 'must' or 'should'.

questions.explanation:
'Would' introduce la consecuencia hipotetica del condicional tipo dos, sin afirmar que ocurra.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that is correct in the zero conditional.

options.text: Water will freeze at zero degrees, so ice would form on the surface.
options.feedback: That mixes the first and second conditionals without reason.

options.text: Water freezes at zero degrees, so ice forms on the surface.
options.feedback: 'If' is not needed for this general truth, and the present simple is correct throughout.

options.text: Water would freeze at zero degrees, so ice had formed on the surface.
options.feedback: That mixes the second and third conditionals.

options.text: Water froze at zero degrees, so ice had formed on the surface.
options.feedback: That describes a single past event, not a general truth.

questions.explanation:
El condicional cero usa presente simple en ambas clausulas y expresa una relacion general.

questions.statement: Look at the question and answer it correctly: 'If you had a chance, what would you do?' The answer should be:
questions.context: Aplicacion del condicional tipo dos, Quito.

options.text: I would visit the Galapagos Islands.
options.feedback: 'Would visit' keeps the hypothetical frame of the question.

options.text: I visited the Galapagos Islands last year.
options.feedback: That answers a question about the past, not about a hypothetical present chance.

options.text: I will visit the Galapagos Islands next year.
options.feedback: 'Will' states a future plan rather than the hypothetical answer.

options.text: I visit the Galapagos Islands every year.
options.feedback: The simple present describes a habit, not a hypothetical situation.

Una respuesta coherente con el condicional tipo dos mantiene la forma hipotetica con 'would'.

options.feedback: 'Were' plus 'would' base is the correct second conditional.

questions.statement: What does 'unless' mean in 'Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus'?

options.text: If you do not hurry
options.feedback: 'Unless' is equivalent to 'if not' plus the base verb.

options.text: If you hurry
options.feedback: That reverses the condition given in the sentence.

options.text: When you hurry
options.feedback: 'When' introduces time, not a negative condition.

options.text: Because you hurry
options.feedback: 'Because' introduces a cause, not a condition.

questions.explanation:
'Unless' equivale a 'if not', de modo que la condicion se invierte respecto de lo que se enuncia.
